title: Microwave ovens don’t work by ‘resonating’ water molecules
body: A popular explanation says microwave ovens use the resonant frequency of water. They don’t: most home ovens run at about 2.45 GHz, far from any sharp resonance of water. Instead, the rapidly flipping electric field keeps twisting water molecules, which have a positive and a negative end, and their jostling turns into heat. This is called dielectric heating, and it works over a broad range of frequencies.
